deep.reconstruction:
Setting: (M,m) is a measure space and f a measurable complex function on it. Grothendieck defines the 'mesure spectrale' μ_f as the image measure f(m), viewed as a Radon measure on C* = C∖{0}. That is, ⟨α,μ_f⟩ = ∫ α∘f dm for continuous compactly supported α on C*.

When μ_f exists: it is defined exactly when m(|f|^{-1}[a,b]) < ∞ for all 0<a<b<∞. So existence depends only on |f|. Removing 0 from C is what allows functions like those in C_0(M), or with infinite-measure support, to have a spectral measure.

Basic properties:
- μ_f is positive.
- It is carried by R* (resp. R+*) iff f is real (resp. positive) off its zero set.
- f on M and g on N are called 'spectrally equivalent' if μ_f = μ_g. In modern terms, they are equimeasurable: they have the same distribution function away from 0.

Examples:
- If {f ≠ 0} has finite measure, μ_f exists and is bounded.
- More generally μ_f exists if m{|f| > ε} < ∞ for every ε > 0, e.g. f ∈ C_0(M). This is the standard hypothesis for the decreasing rearrangement.

Proposition 1 concerns decreasing functions on R+* with Lebesgue measure.
- A positive decreasing φ on R+* has a spectral measure iff φ → 0 at ∞.
- In that case μ_φ is a positive measure on R+* with μ_φ([1,∞)) < ∞.
- Conversely, every positive μ on R+* with ∫_1^∞ dμ < ∞ is the spectral measure of a unique (a.e.) positive decreasing φ.
- Formula (3): t = μ([φ(t),∞)) for a.e. t. So φ is the generalized inverse of the tail function s ↦ μ([s,∞)).

Purpose: this is the setup for the decreasing rearrangement φ_f (next page). There Grothendieck shows that f is equimeasurable with a decreasing function on R+* iff all sets {f ≥ a}, a>0, have finite measure. He then characterizes φ_f by the variational formula φ_f(t) = inf{‖(1−E)f‖_∞ : m(E) ≤ t}. He derives monotonicity, homogeneity, φ_{f+g} ≤ φ_f + φ_g, φ_{fg} ≤ φ_f φ_g (with the usual argument shifts) and ∫ f dm = ∫ φ_f dt, N_p(f) = N_p(φ_f).

This is the commutative prototype of his Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955), 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace'. The inf-formula there is what Fack–Kosaki (1986) later used as 'generalized s-numbers' μ_t(x).
errors: Formula (3), t = ∫_{φ(t)}^∞ dμ 'pour presque tout t', fails if μ has atoms. If μ({s}) > 0, φ equals s on a whole interval of positive length, and (3) fails on that interval. The correct statement is μ(]φ(t),∞[) ≤ t ≤ μ([φ(t),∞[) for all t (with a suitable choice of φ). The next page's description of the exceptional t as those where the integral is 'ambiguous' captures this, but they need not form a null set.
Minor: carried by R* iff f real should read 'f real a.e. on {f≠0}'. The example 'f à support compact et m bornée' is garbled or redundant: finite measure of the support is what matters.

The next-page inequalities φ_{f+g} ≤ φ_f + φ_g and φ_{fg} ≤ φ_f φ_g are false pointwise as written. The correct forms are φ_{f+g}(s+t) ≤ φ_f(s) + φ_g(t), and similarly for products. Possibly the transcription lost the arguments.

ideas.what: Spectral measure of a measurable function as the image measure on C∖{0}, and spectral equivalence = equal image measures
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Bourbaki exp. 113 (1955), 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace'

ideas.what: Bijection between positive decreasing functions on R+* vanishing at ∞ and positive measures μ on R+* with μ([1,∞)) < ∞, via generalized inverse of the tail function
ideas.modern_name: decreasing rearrangement as generalized inverse of the distribution function
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya; standard in rearrangement-invariant space theory (Lorentz, Bennett–Sharpley)

ideas.what: Variational formula for the rearrangement φ_f(t) = inf_{m(E)≤t} ‖(1−E)f‖_∞ (next page), designed to pass to traced von Neumann algebras

deep.surprise_reason: This is a manuscript draft of material Grothendieck published in his 1955 Bourbaki exposé on rearrangements in traced von Neumann algebras. That work is already credited (e.g. by Fack–Kosaki). The 'spectral measure on C*' framing is a pleasant detail but standard; nothing here is new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: Title likely 'Mesures spectrales et réarrangement de fonctions' (plausible; the handwriting is ambiguous).
In (2), 'pour toute fonction continue à support compact sur C*' replaces the struck '[-de fonction-]'.
'Deux[?]' before 'une fonction f' is probably 'Deux fonctions:' or a struck fragment; the sense is 'une fonction f sur M et une fonction g sur N sont dites spectralement équivalentes'.
Example line likely reads 'Si l'ensemble f^{-1}(∁0) est intégrable, alors μ_f existe et est bornée'.
In (3), the parenthetical is 's = φ(t)', i.e. t = ∫_{φ(t)}^∞ dμ(s).
